sections.title: Overview
sections.body: The Administration module is accessible only to Controllers. It is organized into a five-section sidebar — Master Data, Reference Catalogues, Planning & Ranking, Portfolio Hierarchy, and System — covering 24 admin sub-surfaces in total. Every change is logged in the categorised audit trail (8 categories per Cluster D Session D2).

sections.title: 5-Section Sidebar Navigation (v5)
sections.body:
Section 1 · Master Data: Cost Centers, Competence Centers, Lines of Business, Workforce Locations, People, plus Cluster F's Charging Locations, Legal Entities, Regions, Countries, and User Measurement.

Section 2 · Reference Catalogues: Role Types, External Cost Types, Project Dependencies.

Section 3 · Planning & Ranking: Planning Parameters and Tech Navigator Scoring.

Section 4 · Portfolio Hierarchy.

Section 5 · System: Users, Role Permissions, Rate Tables, Workflow Templates, Scheduled Changes, Audit Log.

Sidebar selection persists in `?section=` so deep links survive reload (e.g. `/admin?section=workflow_templates`).

sections.title: Cluster F Master Data (Charging Locations, Legal Entities, Regions, Countries)
sections.body:
**Charging Locations** are Knorr-Bremse charging codes (~90 codes, e.g. DE-MUC-001) used for inter-service distribution and SAP cost flows; each carries division, region, and country attributes. The picker in BTC profile editing groups locations by region and division for fast filtering.

**Legal Entities** (~120 registered companies) roll up many-to-one to a Charging Location and have their own Country attribute for divergence cases (e.g. a German charging location backed by an Austrian legal entity).

**Regions** and **Countries** are simple lookup catalogues. Hover the info icon on each panel header for a definition tooltip per `[F-MD-01]`.

All four panels follow the standard CRUD pattern: list table + create dialog + inline edit + Deactivate (soft delete). Deactivation cascades for downstream usage (e.g. deactivating a Charging Location hides it from the BTC line picker but preserves history).

sections.title: User Measurement Matrix
sections.body:
Sparse year × quarter × S-code × charging-location matrix with row and column totals. Use the period selector (year + quarter) and version selector (Latest import / specific imports) to view a snapshot. CSV upload creates a new version (no overwrite — versioning by import timestamp, so historical snapshots are preserved).

The **Automatic refresh** button is intentionally stubbed in the demo: it returns 'not connected to a UM source' as an explanatory dialog rather than a network error, preserving the integration boundary for production SAP-API connection.

The matrix is the source of truth for **automatic** BTC profiles per `[F-S2-03]`. Refreshing an automatic profile (`Refresh from UM` in the Charging module) snapshots the current matrix into the profile's lines.

sections.title: UM CSV import
sections.body:
Step-by-step:
1. Click **Upload CSV** in the User Measurement panel.
2. The file picker accepts a CSV in the documented columns (`year`, `quarter`, `s_code`, `charging_location_code`, `value`).
3. After upload the import dialog shows the result: number of cells inserted, errors per row (if any), and the new version's import timestamp.
4. Switch the version selector to the new timestamp to view the imported snapshot, or stay on **Latest import** to keep the freshest pointer.

Imports are **append-only**: the engine never overwrites prior versions. To rebuild from scratch, re-seed the demo via `POST /api/admin/reset-demo`.

sections.title: Workflow Templates
sections.body:
Six configurable workflows ship: **Forecast Cycle** (5 steps), **Intake / Pipeline Progression** (5), **Change Request** (4), **Send Back** (3), **Milestone Baseline Override** (3), **Scheduled Master Data Activation** (3).

Step sequence is fixed (admin cannot reorder); per-step touchpoints are editable: required / skippable, assigned role, data gates (comma-separated completeness criteria), notifications (JSON object — trigger ➜ recipients, e.g. `{"on_start": ["all_pls"]}`), time-constraint days, and escalation action.

**To edit a step's touchpoint**: pick the template tab → click the step header to expand the edit panel → change values → click Save. An *Unsaved* badge highlights dirty steps; saves persist immediately.

The whole template can be toggled Active/Inactive from the template header card — useful for retiring a workflow without deleting it.

Templates ship as configurable data only in v5; live workflow execution wiring (i.e., enforcing the gates at runtime) is a follow-on session.

sections.title: Scheduled Changes
sections.body:
Future-dated master-data and parameter changes pending review or activation. **5-state lifecycle**: `pending_review` → `approved` → `activated` (or `rejected` / `cancelled`).

**Per-row actions** (visible by status):
- *Pending Review*: Approve (with optional comments) → Approved · Reject (with required reason) → Rejected · Cancel → Cancelled.
- *Approved*: Cancel (still cancellable until activation).
- *Activated / Rejected / Cancelled*: terminal states, no further actions.

The **Apply due changes** button (top-right) manually triggers the activation engine. It scans approved changes whose activation_date has passed and applies each to the live entity. In v5 only **planning_parameter** activation is wired through to the live entity; other entity types record the activation as a no-op (useful for the demo, but requires production wiring before adoption).

**Creation note**: v5 has no UI for *creating* a scheduled change — POST `/api/admin/scheduled-changes` with `{entity_type, entity_id, description, pending_values, activation_date}` directly. activation_date must be today-or-future (past corrections are immediate edits, not scheduled changes).

sections.title: Audit Log V2
sections.body:
Categorised audit entries across all admin actions. **Eight categories** per Cluster D Session D2:
- `master_data` — entity CRUD (people, cost centres, charging locations, etc.)
- `configuration` — planning parameters, workflow template touchpoints
- `hierarchy` — portfolio hierarchy entity types, hierarchies, assignments
- `forecast_actions` — cycle close, CR approval
- `pipeline_transitions` — DoI advances, project pipeline-stage transitions
- `simulator` — scenario create / publish / promote / archive
- `access_control` — role permission grants and BTC / distribution gate changes
- `scheduled_change_lifecycle` — scheduled change reviews and activations

Filter by category, entity type, and date range. Each entry shows the timestamp, user, entity, action, and an old → new diff column. Export the filtered set to CSV or Excel via the buttons in the panel header (`audit_export.py` builds the CSV).

Retention: indefinite in v5 (audit log is never deleted).

sections.title: Role Permissions Grid
sections.body:
Per-role × per-entity-type permission grants for **BTC Profile** and **Stage 1 Distribution** edits, plus generic master-data overrides per `[F-AC-01]`.

**Default behaviour**: the responsible person on the entity owns the entity (can edit). The Controller has audit-trailed override authority. Other roles have no edit rights by default.

**To add a grant**: pick the role × entity-type cell, click + Add grant, scope to a specific entity_id (or leave blank for role-wide), choose action level (read/edit/delete), save. Changes affect BTC profile + distribution edit gates immediately on save and are recorded in the audit log under category `access_control`.

**Tier 3 gating**: Tier 3 scenario actions (Lever 10 / Lever 11 — cost-allocation) require both `tier3_flag=true` on the user AND a matching `RolePermissionGrant`. Controllers default-have these grants; other roles need explicit grants.

sections.title: Tech Navigator Scoring
sections.body:
Section 3 of the admin sidebar (Planning & Ranking) has a dedicated **Tech Navigator Scoring** page that surfaces the full backlog scoring formula with live controls.

**Layout (top to bottom):**
- *Formula card* — read-only display of the composite formula: composite = (V·wV + X·wC) / (wV + wC), where V is the Value Creation axis score (weighted average of Financial benefit, Payback, Competitive advantage) and X is the Complexity axis score (weighted average of Standardization, Usage, Maintenance).
- *Composite mixer* — wV and wC (defaults 70 / 30).
- *Complexity axis* — Standardization, Usage, Maintenance (defaults 40 / 40 / 20).
- *Value Creation axis* — Financial benefit, Payback, Competitive advantage (defaults 50 / 40 / 10).
- *T-shirt size thresholds (EUR)* — XS ≤ 100 000 · S ≤ 250 000 · M ≤ 500 000 · L ≤ 1 000 000 · XL above.
- *Backlog cutoff envelope* — Total Available Budget (default 14 440 000 €) that sets the should-be / reality cutoff lines on the Backlog page.
- *Live preview — Tech Navigator quadrant* — a scatter chart of every backlog/operate project plotted at (Value Creation, Complexity), with dot colour reflecting composite (low grey → high emerald), dot size reflecting T-shirt, and a dashed diagonal **iso-composite line** at the should-be cutoff threshold. As you drag any slider, the chart recomputes client-side and the dots / iso-line move in real time — no save required to preview.

**Controls:** each weight has a slider + number input synced two-ways. Drag for visual feel; type for precision. The sum indicator in each axis header turns amber if the values no longer add to 100 (informational only — the formula normalizes by the sum, so any non-negative weights work).

**Save / Reset:** the page tracks a working state separate from the saved server state. The Save button enables when any value differs. On save, a single bulk write applies all dirty rows and the backend automatically recomputes every project's composite_score / value_creation_score / complexity_score / tshirt_size (and the within_cutoff flag, if you also changed the budget envelope). Reset all returns every value to its hardcoded default. All changes are written to the audit log under the `configuration` category.

**Behavioural quirk to know about:** the seed.sql hardcodes some project score literals that don't exactly match what the formula would produce from the same sub-criteria. The first time you save any tn_* edit, the auto-recompute hook normalizes those literals, so a few projects' composite scores may shift by ~0.05 even when you change the weights back to defaults. This is a one-time effect tied to seed precision, not the formula.

sections.title: Project Dependencies
sections.body:
Define inter-project dependency relationships used by the Backlog ranker for cross-project conflict detection. Each dependency has a source project, a target project, and a type (`depends_on`, `blocks`, `related_to`).

Dependencies surface as warnings on the Backlog detail page when the source project is funded but the target is below the cutoff line. They do not auto-cascade ranking, but they alert the controller to potential sequencing problems before Pitch Board.

Per the standard CRUD pattern: list, create, deactivate. Deactivating preserves the row in `audit_log` (`master_data` category).

sections.title: Entity Type Selector (left rail)
sections.body:
The left panel organizes manageable items into the five sidebar groups described above. Section 1 (Master Data) holds the largest concentration of CRUD panels — the v4 entity catalogues (Cost Centers, Competence Centers, Lines of Business, Workforce Locations, People) are joined by Cluster F's master data (Charging Locations, Legal Entities, Regions, Countries, User Measurement). Section 5 (System) is where the workflow / scheduled-change / audit / role-permission tooling lives.

Click any item to load its management panel on the right. The current selection is reflected in the URL `?section=` parameter.

sections.title: CRUD Operations
sections.body: For each entity type, you can create new entries, edit existing ones, and deactivate records. **Important:** {app_name} uses deactivation instead of deletion — deactivated records are hidden from active views but preserved for historical accuracy. Deactivation may cascade (e.g., deactivating a cost center affects its people).

sections.title: Cost Center Management
sections.body: Create cost centers with a name, location, and competence center assignment. Edit to change assignments. Deactivate to remove from active views while preserving allocation history.

sections.title: People Management
sections.body: Add people with name, role type, and cost center assignment. Edit to transfer between cost centers or change roles. Deactivate when someone leaves. The system preserves all historical allocations and cost calculations.

sections.title: Users
sections.body:
The Users panel manages the human accounts behind personas. Each user has a name, e-mail, optional `tier3_flag` (controls access to Tier 3 scenario content per `[B-SL-03]`), and an `is_active` flag. The DemoPersona table maps each demo persona to a User; switching persona in the demo header swaps the X-Current-User used on every request.

In production the Users panel would be the integration point for SSO; in v5 the panel is read-only and the personas are seeded.

sections.title: Rate Table Management
sections.body:
View and update hourly rates per role per competence center. When updating a rate, set the **new effective date** (must be today or future). The system preserves the previous rate and effective date for audit purposes — historical cost calculations always use the rate that was in effect at the time.

The rate-in-effect for any given month is the latest RateTable row with `effective_from ≤ month`. Past corrections are out-of-scope for this panel; they require a different remediation flow.

sections.title: Portfolio Hierarchy Management
sections.body:
The Portfolio Hierarchy panel (under Portfolio Structure) lets you configure how projects are grouped across the application. It has four sub-tabs:

**Entity Types** — Define grouping categories such as Line of Business, Programme, or Division. Each type has a name and optional description.

**Hierarchies** — Arrange entity types into ordered levels to form a tree structure. One hierarchy can be marked as **Active** — this determines the grouping used across all modules. Only one hierarchy can be active at a time.

**Grouping Entities** — Create and manage the actual entities within each type (e.g., 'Truck & Bus Systems' under Line of Business, 'Rail Signalling' under Programme). Set parent-child relationships between entities of different types.

**Hierarchy Assignment** — View the active hierarchy as a tree and see which projects are assigned to which entities. Drag or reassign projects between entities.

The active hierarchy's labels propagate across **Portfolio Overview** (tree grouping and filters), **Capacity Management** (pivot dimensions), **Project Workbench** (entity selector fields), and **Reporting** (filter and dimension labels).

sections.title: Planning Parameters
sections.body:
Configure system-wide settings organized into six groups:

**Fiscal Settings** — Fiscal Year Start Month.
**Planning Horizon** — Number of planning years ahead.
**Thresholds** — RAG thresholds (Amber and Red percentages for variance-based status calculations) plus t-shirt size budget thresholds.
**Limits** — Maximum Scenarios per User and other system caps.
**Capacity Settings** — Target Utilization percentage for capacity planning, plus heatmap colour-band cutoffs.
**Integrations** — API key management for external services. The Anthropic API key (used by the AI Report Builder) is stored here as a secret parameter with masked display. Use the **eye icon** to temporarily reveal the key value.

Each group has its own **Save** and **Reset to Defaults** controls. Editing a `tn_*` or `tshirt_*` parameter triggers a portfolio-wide Tech Navigator score and t-shirt size recompute.

sections.title: Audit Trail
sections.body: All administrative changes are logged with timestamp, who made the change, what entity was affected, the specific field changed, and old/new values. The audit log is visible at the bottom of the Administration module (Section 5 · System · Audit Log) and supports the 8-category filter described under Audit Log V2.
